body:
ARGUMENT BEFORE THE EDIT on bd-01M16C9HT9V9Q80F7411V87BBY part 2, as you asked. I AGREE WITH YOUR LEAN - the default becomes Missing - and here is the case, plus the facts I verified rather than assumed.

FACTS. NodeSummary.importance defaults to Estimate.observed(1.0) (source.scala:109). StorySourceView - the production bridge from a story model - constructs NodeSummary WITHOUT passing importance (StorySourceView.scala:98), so every node in every production run carries observed(1.0). The only places that ever set it are three test call sites. So importanceWeightedCoverage = sum(1.0 * visitation) / sum(1.0) = mean visitation = uniformCoverage, identically, in every production run this library has ever done.

WHY MISSING RATHER THAN A DECLARED UNIFORM PRIOR.

1. observed(1.0) IS AN ASSERTION AND WE MEASURED NOTHING. Estimate.observed means we have a value for this quantity. We do not have a salience for these nodes; nobody supplied one. That is the same defect the whole night has been about - a default standing where evidence should be - and it is worse here than usual because the default is not a neutral zero but a claim of MAXIMAL salience for every node simultaneously.

2. THE DECLARED-PRIOR OPTION DOES NOT ACTUALLY FIX THE PROBLEM, which is why I would reject it even though it is defensible in principle. Declaring "absent importances mean a uniform prior" makes the equality expected rather than discovered - but the library still publishes TWO NAMED FIELDS THAT ARE THE SAME NUMBER. A researcher reading a signature sees uniformCoverage and importanceWeightedCoverage, and reasonably infers two measurements. A footnote saying they coincide when no importances are supplied does not undo the inference; it just means we told them somewhere. If someone wants the uniform figure, uniformCoverage IS that figure and is honestly named.

3. MISSING IS ACTIONABLE WHERE A DUPLICATE IS NOT. Under Missing, a caller who supplies no importances is told: this quantity was not measured. That is true, and it is the thing they need to know to decide whether to supply importances. Today they are handed a number that looks like an independent measurement and silently is not.

THE COST, STATED PLAINLY: importanceWeightedCoverage becomes Missing in every current production run, which is a visible change to any consumer reading it. I think that is exactly right - the field was never a distinct measurement - but it is a real behaviour change and not a no-op refactor, and the type's own Scaladoc already says "Missing importance excludes the node from importance-weighted coverage; it is never zero", so the semantics for handling it exist and are documented.

PART 1 IS NOT CONTINGENT and I am doing it regardless: `if wsum <= 0 then uniform` silently republishes the uniform figure under the importance-weighted name when every importance is Missing. That becomes Missing with a reason.

Implementing both now on that basis; reverse me on part 2 and I will restore the default in one line.
